## Program descriptions

- **MathOverflow (not formalized)** — Open questions asked by research mathematicians on MathOverflow, still without an accepted answer.
- **OEIS conjectures (not formalized)** — Conjectures stated in the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences that are not marked proved or refuted. Often testable by computation first.
- **arXiv abstracts (not formalized)** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Erdős Problems** — Paul Erdős's problems, many with cash prizes, as catalogued on erdosproblems.com by Thomas Bloom.
- **Wikipedia** — Problems from Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics.
- **OEIS** — Conjectures attached to sequences in the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences. Often numerically explorable.
- **Mathematics Stack Exchange (not formalized)** — Open questions from Mathematics Stack Exchange, still without an accepted answer.
- **Wikipedia list (not formalized)** — Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems and list of conjectures: everything not yet stated in Lean. Step one is a faithful statement.
- **Open Problem Garden** — Problems from the Open Problem Garden wiki (graph theory, combinatorics, number theory…), not yet stated in Lean.
- **Green's 100 Open Problems** — Ben Green's list of 100 open problems in additive combinatorics and related areas.
- **Papers** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Erdős Problems (not formalized)** — Open Erdős problems that nobody has stated in Lean yet.
- **arXiv papers** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Wikipedia (not formalized)** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Open Quantum Problems** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Optimization Constants** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Written on the Wall II** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Other** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Books** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **MathOverflow** — Questions from MathOverflow that are still open.
- **Millennium Prize** — The Clay Millennium Prize problems that can be stated in Lean today, with nearby conjectures.
- **Kourovka Notebook** — Unsolved problems in group theory from the Kourovka Notebook.
- **Hilbert's Problems** — What remains open of Hilbert's 1900 list.
- **Open problems in information theory (gokhanmergen)** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Conjectures of Luc Gillibert** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.
- **Litt's Problems** — Open problems stated in research papers and books.

## Method, licensing carve-out & guards

- **Crawl etiquette:** Public `/api/problems`, `/api/stats` and `/programs` endpoints (all permitted by `robots.txt`; disallowed `/api/desk/` and `/api/verdict` are never touched), fetched once per day with an identifying User-Agent, 0.35 s delay and exponential back-off.
- **Metadata only + licensing carve-out:** Each JSONL record stores `id`, `title`, `kind`, `fields`, `prize`, and `solved` only — zero statement excerpts, zero volatile counters. Any program exceeding 4 MiB is sharded into `.part-001.jsonl`, `.part-002.jsonl`, … to stay strictly under the 5 MB Build Standard A24 cap. Third-party titles remain under their upstream sources' licenses (Apache-2.0 / CC BY-SA 4.0 / OEIS / OPG); `data/external/lefttosolve/` is explicitly carved out of this repository's CC BY 4.0 data license (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).
- **Fail-closed guards:** Sync aborts without writing if fewer than 10 programs parse, fetched completeness is < 99.5%, any per-program count fails reconciliation, or mirrored items shrink by > 20%.
- **Offline integrity:** `python scripts/sync_external_programs.py --check` recomputes the full-catalogue SHA-256 over all 59k+ items, verifies every shard stays < 5 MB, and checks every generated view offline.
